clue.text: Peruvian Indians can be found in Casas Grandes ruins

indicators.note: can be found says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows, across a word break

explanation.surface: A note that Peruvian natives turn up among the ruins of Casas Grandes, a Mexican archaeological site.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'in' into the start of 'Casas'; 'Grandes ruins' only dresses the surface, and 'ruins' is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people ruled an empire centred on Peru before the Spanish conquest.

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of the two words are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone who is a fool may be amusing, or may not be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' looks like 'or not', but it tells you to rearrange AMUSING and OR together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant, foolish person is a dunce, a synonym for a fool.

definitions.meaning: low-value copper-coloured coins, small change
slang for police officers, the police force

explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are both bronze coins of small value and, in British slang, police officers.

clue.text: Thus taught to make consomme, perhaps

parts.note: thus means so, in that way
to be up on a subject is to be well taught in it, knowledgeable

explanation.surface: A cookery lesson: this is how you are taught to make a clear broth.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'taught' is the sense of being well up in a subject. 'perhaps' marks consomme as one example of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: Consomme is a clear broth, one kind of a liquid dish served from a bowl.

clue.text: Silly chap to be so close to striker

definitions.text: Silly chap to be so close to striker

parts.words: Silly chap to be so close to striker
parts.note: in cricket, 'silly' positions such as silly point are fielding spots very close to the batsman, the striker

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a fool is foolish to stand so near an attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' looks like an insult, but in cricket a silly position is a fielding place right beside the batsman (the striker); a fielder there is a close-in player.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket player stationed near the batsman, in a close position, fits the description of a close fielder.

parts.note: the outlook is what lies ahead, the time to come
ideal means flawless, without fault

explanation.surface: Prospects look excellent, yet someone still feels nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective meaning anxious, but it is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical form 'will have done' is a verb tense in English grammar.

clue.text: Flair for some of the languages

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has a gift for picking up foreign tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is a French-derived word for dash, style or vigour, close to flair.

clue.text: Catch sight of record English fleet

parts.note: a record is a disc, as in a vinyl record
RN, the Royal Navy, is Britain's naval fleet

explanation.surface: Someone spots an old record of England's navy.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, the UK's naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something with the eyes is to perceive or spot it, which is the verb's meaning.

definitions.meaning: in printing, the ordinary upright typeface as opposed to italic
in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Mark Antony begins his speech 'Friends, ..., countrymen'

explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the upright printing typeface, and Mark Antony's famous speech addresses the citizens of Rome.

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a melody is a tune

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a tune taken from Holst's orchestral suite The Planets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Planets' is Gustav Holst's orchestral suite, each movement named after a planet; the definition is one movement from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's suite closes with a movement named after the eighth planet, the mystic sea god of the solar system.

clue.text: Volume turned up in ice-dance a ploy to confuse!

indicators.note: to confuse is to mix up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A big book appears at an ice-dancing contest as a ploy to unsettle rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up in' is link text meaning 'appeared as'; 'to confuse' tells you to rearrange ICEDANCE, A and PLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference work of many articles often fills a large book, which is one sense of volume.

indicators.note: a rout is a disorderly defeat, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A soldier from the cross ranks at the Battle of Marston Moor, a Civil War rout.
explanation.walkthrough: Marston Moor (1644) was a crushing English Civil War defeat for the Royalists; 'rout' tells you to rearrange MARSTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal crossbar in a window or door frame is a structural beam, a crosswise member.

clue.text: Animal runs back in long grass

indicators.note: runs back says the word for the creature is read from end to start

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature dashes back into tall grass to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs back' tells you to write DEER backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall waterside plant with hollow stems is a grass-like plant found in marshes.

clue.text: Nick with a bone to pick?

definitions.meaning: to nick is to cut a notch or scratch
someone with a bone to pick has a grievance

explanation.definitionFit: To score is to scratch a line, and an old grudge to settle is called a score.

indicators.note: seen in says the answer is visible within the following words, across the comma

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes which bird usually appears in the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'winter' into the start of 'normally'.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird, related to gulls, has a forked tail.

definitions.meaning: excursions are trips or outings
a French city on the river Loire

explanation.definitionFit: Tours are trips, and Tours is a French city on the Loire.

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was the first Tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: A duke is called a dreadful man for the way he behaves in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible fellow' points to Ivan the Terrible, the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: A low couch without back or arms, often used as a sofa or for sleeping.

clue.text: Spilling of pints economic? That's a fallacy

indicators.note: spilling scatters things, so the letters of the following words are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone claims that spilling beer saves money; another calls it a false belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilling of' tells you to rearrange PINTS and ECONOMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistaken belief or false idea is the meaning of a fallacy.

clue.text: What could come from Clydesdale that could end in a bow?

definitions.text: What could come from Clydesdale that could end in a bow?

parts.words: What could come from Clydesdale that could end in a bow?
parts.note: a Clydesdale is a Scottish draught animal; strands from its tail are used to string a violin bow

explanation.walkthrough: A Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of draught animal; 'bow' looks like a ribbon knot but is a violin bow, strung with tail strands.
explanation.definitionFit: Violin bows are strung with long tail strands taken from the animal, so the material comes from a Clydesdale.

parts.note: read literally, an official with authority over a port, such as the person in charge of a dock

explanation.walkthrough: 'Port authority' usually names an organisation; read literally it is the officer who runs a port.
explanation.definitionFit: The official responsible for a dock's shipping and berths has command over the port.

clue.text: Glory be! Governess supports bottomless stockings!

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
bottomless means the last letter, at the bottom of the word, is taken away

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings
Anna Leonowens was the governess in The King and I

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight when a governess holds up stockings with no feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottomless' cuts the last letter of HOSE; 'supports' puts ANNA under HOS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of praise to God, like the shout heard on Palm Sunday.

definitions.meaning: powerful in the sense of striking or effective, as an argument
reporting means recounting, relating a story

explanation.definitionFit: A striking point is said to be forceful or effective, and recounting a story is narrating it.

definitions.meaning: fair means equitable
only means merely, simply
now as in a moment ago
lawful means rightful, legitimate

explanation.definitionFit: The word means equitable, merely, a moment ago and rightful, covering all four clue words.

clue.text: Esau's brother Bill is in work

indicators.note: is in places the short abbreviation inside the word for employment

parts.note: a job is work
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Esau's sibling has his bill tucked into his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau's twin took his birthright and blessing.

parts.note: in Genesis Cain is called the slayer of his brother, so the clue points to that victim

explanation.surface: A man who killed a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'slayer of' to lead to the brother Cain killed, a loose pointer.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so any bearer of it is a female person.

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A fighter's first move is to take shelter while running away.
explanation.walkthrough: LEE is the sheltered side away from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger is to bolt, a synonym for making an escape.

definitions.meaning: to reserve a seat or table is to engage it in advance
a printed volume that is published

explanation.definitionFit: To engage a table in advance is to arrange it, and a printed volume is a publication.

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: A calm feeling in the air before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, the musical marking for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that go together form a couple, a matching set of two.

definitions.meaning: harmony means agreement, accord
a historic town in Massachusetts, site of an early battle of the American Revolution

explanation.definitionFit: The word means agreement or accord, and is the name of a Massachusetts town famed for its 1775 battle.

clue.text: Red Queen observed as train is changed…

indicators.note: is changed says the letters of the preceding words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A Communist monarch is spotted as a railway carriage is swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour or Communist, but here means Russian: the wife of a Tsar. 'is changed' rearranges AS TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a Russian Tsar was the empress of Russia, a queen of the Reds.

clue.text: … the Ace of Spades or the Knave of Clubs?

definitions.text: the Ace of Spades or the Knave of Clubs?

parts.words: the Ace of Spades or the Knave of Clubs?
parts.note: both cards are dark-suited, and an ace with a jack gives the winning twenty-one hand in a casino card game

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's surface. In the casino card game twenty-one, an ace plus a jack wins, and both cards named are dark-suited.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game of twenty-one takes its name from a winning hand of an ace with a dark jack.

definitions.meaning: a man's given name, so a chap
in radio communication the word confirms a message has been received and understood

explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, and the radio operator's reply meaning 'received and understood'.
